recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is recommended for FHIR-5512 unless the work group later decides to revisit the underlying http/https identity policy.
issue_request: FHIR-5512 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core HTTP and asked the specification to clarify whether http versus https and port number are significant factors in determining resource identity. The adopted ITS wording treated http and https as not separate objects, while specified ports remain significant and should be explicit only when meaningful to the server.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 5051, represented in git by d0f47223ad0f368f159e7f2ccbd205234b2fc31f, which added the Identity section to source/http.html. A later related Published/Persuasive issue, FHIR-8683, clarified the protocol wording in cd02a83cb81e816388e258b698d29f8f9b4c49ee without reversing the FHIR-5512 policy.
additional_context: source/http.html is the active RESTful API page through source/hierarchy.xml. The current Identity section states that query strings are ignored, the document portion is case-sensitive, http and https SHALL NOT be used to refer to different underlying objects, and specified ports must be identical or the objects are different. Related audits for FHIR-8683 and FHIR-19668 were already present on the combined branch, and community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already satisfies the requested clarification and later wording changes preserve the same implementer-facing rule.
